#98157. Breaking: BYD’s folding steering wheel isn’t a concept — it’s in a $49K SUV now

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1139 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: BYD’s folding steering wheel isn’t a concept — it’s in a $49K SUV now

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1139 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, BYD released a production SUV today with a steering wheel that folds flat into the dashboard.
  • Sources indicate that automakers and suppliers have been parading folding wheels on concept cars for about a decade.
  • Industry observers note that the whole thing hinges on steer-by-wire.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, BYD released a production SUV today with a steering wheel that folds flat into the dashboard. It comes standard on the top trim of the Fang Cheng Bao Tai 9, which sells for 329,900 yuan (about $49,000) in China.

Sources indicate that automakers and suppliers have been parading folding wheels on concept cars for about a decade. This is the first one customers can actually order, according to BYD.

Industry observers note that the whole thing hinges on steer-by-wire. There’s no steering column physically connecting the wheel to the front wheels, so the wheel is just an input device, and BYD can put it wherever it wants.

On the Tai 9, it swings through 180 degrees on a hidden hinge and drops into a compartment in the dash in about 10 seconds. A panel closes over it, and a tray table folds out where the wheel used to be. Only the airbag remains outside of the compartment – keeping it useful with the steering wheel deployed or hidden.

Industry observers note that it only folds when the vehicle is parked. Fang Cheng Bao pairs it with a driver’s seat that reclines to 165 degrees, so the pitch is simple: fold the wheel, lie back, and eat, nap, or play games while you charge or wait. The brand claims 80% of the driver’s area becomes usable space and rates the folding mechanism for 80,000 cycles.

It has been revealed that when it’s deployed, it’s a regular D-shaped wheel with a full rim and physical buttons. No yoke. That’s a nice change from Tesla and Mercedes, which paired its upcoming steer-by-wire system on the EQS with a yoke.

At the launch event, Fang Cheng Bao general manager Xiong Tianbo said the industry had been talking about folding steering wheels since 2016 without ever getting one into mass production. He added that BYD is using the same type of motor it develops for humanoid robots to move the wheel, a first in one of its cars.

Here’s Fang Cheng Bao’s official video of the feature:.

According to recent reports, china’s new national standard for steering systems took effect on July 1, 2026. It dropped the long-standing requirement for a mechanical link between the steering wheel and the road wheels, as long as the system meets redundancy and fail-safe rules.

Recent findings suggest that before that, steer-by-wire needed special approval. Nio’s ET9 was the first car in China to get it, back in December 2024. In the US, Tesla’s Cybertruck already uses it, and Mercedes is bringing it to the EQS this year.

It has been revealed that folding wheels themselves have stayed on show stands. BYD’s own Denza brand revealed one on the Z concept at Shanghai in 2025. Autoliv and Tensor called theirs the “world’s first foldable steering wheel” at CES in January, for a Tensor Robocar they expected to reach volume production in the second half of 2026. Hyundai Mobis has been showing one for years.

Tesla went the other way with the Cybercab: no wheel at all. But the prototypes testing on public roads have a Cybertruck steering wheel bolted onto an exposed column, because a human still has to be able to drive.

Recent findings suggest that the Tai 9 is Fang Cheng Bao’s biggest SUV yet. It’s 5,270 mm (207.5 in) long with a 3,130 mm wheelbase and six seats in a 2+2+2 layout. It’s also the first model on BYD’s newly introduced DMS hybrid platform.

A 1.5-liter turbo engine works with front and rear electric motors for a combined 400 kW (536 hp), and 0 to 100 km/h takes 4.8 seconds. The 66.48 kWh second-generation Blade battery supports BYD’s flash charging and delivers 310 km (193 miles) of electric range on the WLTC cycle. Rear-wheel steering, LiDAR, and BYD’s God’s Eye B driver assistance system are standard.

There are three trims: 279,900 yuan (about $41,700), 299,900 yuan, and 329,900 yuan. Only the top one gets the folding wheel.

Fang Cheng Bao sold 43,872 vehicles in October, up 41% year-over-year, mostly on the strength of the Tai 7. That model is now heading overseas: BYD sells it in the UK as the Ti 7. BYD hasn’t said anything about exporting the Tai 9.

It is not only that these technologies are impressive, but it is the speed at which they are being put into market by some of these Chinese car companies like BYD. They are moving further and further away from the competition but its understandable with the insane competition between car makers in China that they almost have to maintain and edge.

Sources indicate that we’ve seen this at pretty much every auto show since the mid-2010s: a steering wheel slides away so the “driver” can relax while the car drives itself. It never shipped, for many reasons, but with steer-by-wire and autonomous driving now becoming reality, BYD is making the jump.

Sources indicate that the Tai 9’s wheel only folds when you’re parked, so right now it’s a lounge feature. Recline the seat, stow the wheel, flip out the tray, and watch a movie while you charge. Is that a gimmick? A little. But Chinese EV buyers spend a lot of time in parked cars, and fridges, screens, and lie-flat seats sell cars there for a reason.

Recent findings suggest that the bigger deal is underneath. The wheel can only fold because the Tai 9 is steer-by-wire, and BYD is putting that in a roughly $49,000 family SUV less than five months after China made it legal. After Cybertruck and now Mercedes with the EQS, we might be seeing the first steps of steer-by-wire actually becoming a more widely adopted technology.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • After 16 years of painstaking work, the National Archives and its collaborators have finally completed digitizing over 90,000 pension applications submitted to the United States government following the War of 1812.
  • According to recent reports, while archivists previously digitized a similar collection related to the American Revolutionary War, the upcoming documents will help fill in knowledge gaps between early 19th century military events and the 1850 federal census.
  • “In the specific case of the War of 1812 pension records, there is an added priority due to their frail state where not acting may mean sacrificing these for future generations,” Oxley said in a recent announcement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After 16 years of painstaking work, the National Archives and its collaborators have finally completed digitizing over 90,000 pension applications submitted to the United States government following the War of 1812. The project is more than just preservation for preservation’s sake. The roughly 2.8 million pages contain long-forgotten and missing details about 19th century Americans, their families, and their everyday lives.

According to recent reports, while archivists previously digitized a similar collection related to the American Revolutionary War, the upcoming documents will help fill in knowledge gaps between early 19th century military events and the 1850 federal census. Patricia Oxley, president of the Federation of Genealogical Societies (FGS), explained the project was also incredibly time-sensitive.

“In the specific case of the War of 1812 pension records, there is an added priority due to their frail state where not acting may mean sacrificing these for future generations,” Oxley said in a recent announcement.

It has been revealed that the somewhat upcoming United States of America declared war on the United Kingdom on June 18, 1812, citing objections to trade restrictions with France amid the Napoleonic Wars, as well as the Royal Navy’s impressment of American sailors. Although the conflict famously included a British attack on Washington D.C. that resulted in the burning of the White House and U.S. Capitol, little shifted geopolitically between the two nations following the ratification of the Treaty of Ghent on February 17, 1815. The U.S. tallied around 15,000 casualties, while the U.K. and Canada saw about 10,700 deaths. Another 9,000 Indigenous fighters died while enlisted between the two sides.

Today’s military records are meticulously documented and stored digitally, but applying for benefits such as pensions was a much more labor-intensive process during the 19th century. With the burden of proof on each applicant, veterans were required to supply lengthy accounts of their service. Each War of 1812 pension file is liable to contain not just combat information, but the names and personal details of fellow soldiers, family members, spouses, and countless other relations.

“Our users have been asking for the War of 1812 pension records for some time, and I expect this collection to be very popular based on the rich war time detail it contains,” added Brian Hansen, general manager at Fold3, Ancestry’s military records service and National Archives collaborator.

Sources indicate that the collection also includes a full-text search feature using handwriting recognition technology. This lets owners explore the files based on every named individual, and not simply the primary veteran applicants. The pension records are presently available for free on Fold3’s website, and are being added to the National Archives catalog on a rolling basis.

According to recent reports, correction 11/20/26 9:30 a.m. EST: A previous version of this article incorrectly stated the pension archive contained around 7 million files. This was based on an initial assessment from researchers in 2010. The article has been updated to reflect the more accurate tally.

It has been revealed that if this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying newly introduced.

Sources indicate that the Temerario's powertrain consists of a twin-turbo 4.0-liter V-8 with a flat-plane crankshaft, a trio of axial-flux electric motors, and an eight-speed dual-clutch transmission. The Temerario's V-8 alone is good for 789 horsepower; adding the output of the three electric motors brings the total combined output to 907 horsepower. That's just 94 ponies shy of the Lamborghini Revuelto, the brand's V-12 halo car. On the Temerario, one electric motor mounts to the V-8 in front of the transmission, while the remaining two live up front, one at each wheel. The Temerario's V-8 redlines at 10,000 rpm, and the engine's peak torque of 538 pound-feet is available from 4000 to 7000 rpm. While the flat-plane-crank V-8 sounds glorious when pushed to its limit, we wish that its exhaust packed a bit more fury earlier in the rev range.

According to recent reports, with the electric motors in play, maximum torque output rises to 590 pound-feet. In addition to supplying enormous power, the hybrid configuration helps provide instantaneous torque and linear power delivery over a broad range of speeds and driving situations. Thirteen drive programs are available via a rotary button on the steering wheel, including launch and drift modes, the latter offering three levels of tail-out leeway. We drove the Temerario at the track and on the street and were enthralled with its lively powertrain and playful demeanor.

Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.

According to recent reports, in Comparison: In our testing, the Temerario got to 60 mph in a ridiculously quick 2.1 seconds. It also ripped through the quarter-mile in 9.4 seconds at 150 miles per hour. Both figures beat its major sibling, the Revuelto, by 0.3 seconds and 2 mph, respectively.

Industry observers note that juice is stored in a 3.8-kWh lithium-ion battery pack. The battery resides in the center tunnel along with the transmission—the location is remarked to help optimize weight distribution and is protected from underneath by structural elements. Regenerative braking and power from the internal-combustion engine both replenish the battery's state of charge. Plug-in charging is also possible via a standard 7-kW onboard charger; with typical household current, it can recharge an empty battery to full capacity in a claimed 30 minutes. An EV-only mode provides around 4 miles of range.

According to recent reports, the EPA estimates that the Temerario will deliver 14 mpg city, 19 mpg highway, and 16 mpg combined. When we get a chance to test the Temerario, we'll update this story with results from our 75-mph highway fuel economy test. For more information about the Temerario's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.

According to recent reports, first Row: Thanks to its all-aluminum chassis, the Temerario's interior offers more space than the Huracán it replaced. Headroom increased by 1.3 inches, legroom by 1.8 inches, and Lamborghini claims the interior is large enough to accommodate drivers up to six feet five wearing a helmet. The interior shares some styling cues from the Revuelto; four stitching patterns are available, and the 18-way adjustable driver's seat is heated and ventilated. The Temerario also borrows the Revuelto's steering wheel, which is too busy with controls for our liking.

Cargo Capacity: If you're planning on taking the Temerario on a weekend getaway, you'd better pack light; the front trunk only has a four-cubic-foot capacity.

Lamborghini says the Temerario offers the most advanced suite of infotainment and connectivity features of any model in its lineup. Three displays—a 12.3-inch instrument panel with three user-selectable views, an 8.4-inch infotainment screen, and a 9.1-inch passenger screen—occupy prime dashboard real estate. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, as is a Sonus Faber audio system.

In a recent development, the most notable feature, though, is the optional Lamborghini Vision Unit (LAVU) system. Essentially an on-board data acquisition system, the setup utilizes three cameras: one viewing the road, one focused on the passengers, and one looking forward over the driver's shoulder. Preloaded with data for 150 different racing circuits, the system can be used to evaluate and improve driver performance. It also enables a "memories recorder" function that allows for up to two minutes of off-track recording, and works as a dashcam that can capture one minute of incident history.

Compared to most other cars, the Temerario doesn't offer many driver-assistance features.

For information about the Temerario's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

According to recent reports, compared with most mainstream automakers, Lamborghini doesn't provide stellar warranty coverage. But its protection plans are competitive with those of high-end rivals such as Ferrari and can be enhanced by optional extended coverage. A five-year complimentary scheduled maintenance proposal is now standard.

#98154. Latest Update: U.S. Loses Measles-Free Status After 26 Years, a Major Public Health Setback

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1343 w)

Latest Update: U.S. Loses Measles-Free Status After 26 Years, a Major Public Health Setback

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1343 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The United States has officially lost its measles elimination status, a major public health achievement that was secured 26 years ago.
  • The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), the World Health Organization’s (WHO) regional office for the Americas, determined that measles has spread continuously in the U.S.
  • According to recent reports, “Losing a measles elimination status has broader implications than losing a public health designation,” PAHO’s director, Jarbas Barbosa, MD, MPH, PhD, noted in a media briefing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The United States has officially lost its measles elimination status, a major public health achievement that was secured 26 years ago.

The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), the World Health Organization’s (WHO) regional office for the Americas, determined that measles has spread continuously in the U.S. for more than 12 months. On November 17, PAHO confirmed the end of the country’s measles elimination status, which it has held since 2000.

According to recent reports, “Losing a measles elimination status has broader implications than losing a public health designation,” PAHO’s director, Jarbas Barbosa, MD, MPH, PhD, noted in a media briefing. “It means the virus has circulated for a prolonged period of time, putting families and communities at risk of a preventable illness, hospitalization, and death.”.

PAHO’s review examined measles spread starting January 20, 2025, when the first person became ill in a large West Texas outbreak, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

CDC data show 5,412 confirmed measles cases this year as of November 12. That’s the highest annual total since 1991 and more than double the 2025 count of 2,289 cases.

Andi Shane, MD, chief of pediatric infectious diseases at Children’s Healthcare of Atlanta, called the U.S. losing measles elimination status “a public health alarm that we are not being effective and we’re not controlling measles as well.”.

Industry observers note that the measles virus is highly contagious. It spreads through the air when an infected person coughs or sneezes. People can catch it in a room up to two hours after an infected person has left, according to the CDC.

“There’s really been very little measles in the United States over the past 25 years until January 2025,” William Moss, MD, a professor of epidemiology at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, told Healthline.

In a recent development, losing the status itself doesn’t change much about daily life for most Americans, Moss remarked. The concern is the measles outbreaks, hospitalizations and deaths behind the loss, he said.

He called the loss “a significant red flag” after “enormous efforts over the past 26 years” to keep the status.

Industry observers note that A country loses its elimination status when there is “uninterrupted circulation of the same virus genotype and lineage for 12 months or more,” according to PAHO. Shane explained it this way: “For the past 12 months in the United States, we’ve had ongoing circulation of the measles virus and person-to-person transmission is occurring.”.

Industry observers note that canada lost its elimination status in November 2025, and the U.K. and five European countries lost theirs earlier in 2026.

Industry observers note that the U.S. can regain the status. “Other countries have done that,” Moss stated. Brazil, which lost its status in 2019, regained it in November 2024. Venezuela, which lost its status in 2018, regained it in 2023, according to PAHO.

According to recent reports, before the measles vaccine, measles infected an estimated 3 million to 4 million Americans each year, according to the CDC. Among reported cases, about 400 to 500 people died each year, 48,000 needed hospital care, and 1,000 developed encephalitis, or brain swelling.

Here’s a timeline of measles elimination in the U.S.:.

In a recent development, moss stated elimination efforts “really intensified” after a large outbreak from 1989 to 1992. Part of that push was “really promoting school entry vaccination checks,” he said.

“That was one of the key policy changes that I think allowed for measles elimination in the United States.”.

Every state and Washington, D.C., require children to be vaccinated against measles to attend school, though exemptions vary by state, according to the nonprofit health policy organization KFF.

Fewer kindergartners are getting the MMR vaccine, according to the CDC.

Recent findings suggest that kindergarten MMR coverage fell from 95.2% in the 2019–2020 school year to 92.4% in 2025–2026. About 280,000 kindergartners started the 2025–2026 school year without records showing they had completed the MMR series, the CDC reported.

Shane said “95 out of 100 people need to be protected against measles” for a community to get herd protection.

“So since we’ve been below that for many, many months, that is also contributing to the loss of our elimination status,” she said.

“It takes two things to have a measles outbreak,” Moss mentioned. A community needs low vaccine coverage, and someone with measles has to enter it and “start the chain of transmission,” he said.

About 96% of this year’s cases were among people who were unvaccinated or had unknown vaccination status, up from 93% in 2025, according to the CDC.

Moss said many of those cases are adults.

It has been revealed that “This is particularly true in Pennsylvania, where about two-thirds of the cases are in adults,” he stated. Many never got vaccinated as kids and grew up while measles was rare, so they never built natural immunity, he said.

He noted that having so many unvaccinated adults puts pregnant people and adults with chronic conditions like lung disease at risk of serious illness. The U.S. has already seen “dozens of pregnant women actually getting infected during pregnancy,” he remarked.Infected parents can also spread measles to young children and grandparents, Shane said. Shane traced much of the hesitancy to the pandemic. “With COVID there’s been an overall distrust in vaccines and vaccination that initially started with COVID but has now spread to other vaccines,” she said.

Sources indicate that moss pointed to the federal government. “We know what it takes to achieve and sustain elimination. We have the expertise. We have the resources,” he noted.

He cited staff cuts at the CDC and noted messaging from Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and President Donald Trump has undermined vaccine confidence. He called federal messaging on vaccines “really mixed and weak.”.

Moss also criticized the President’s August 10 executive order calling for the MMR vaccine to be split into separate shots for each disease.

“There’s no justification for that, and those vaccines don’t even exist in the United States,” he mentioned.

Sources indicate that measles may cause ear infections, diarrhea, pneumonia, encephalitis and, in some cases, death, according to the CDC. The disease may also weaken the immune system for weeks to a year after recovery, raising the risk of flu, COVID-19, or RSV, Shane said. “It’s not a benign childhood disease,” Moss said.

According to recent reports, the best protection against measles is two doses of the MMR vaccine, which are about 97% effective, according to the CDC. Shane said, “There are not very many other things we do in life that give you such great protection.” People who missed doses can still catch up, she added. “If you just don’t know or can’t tell, there’s no harm — as long as you’re eligible — in getting another MMR vaccine.”.

Shane added that “parents really want to do the right thing for their children.”.

“We know that the MMR vaccine — that’s the vaccine that provides protection against measles — is a safe vaccine. It’s a very effective vaccine,” Shane remarked.

Babies under 12 months are too young for the vaccine. “So they depend on the protection of the people around them,” Shane mentioned.

In a recent development, the CDC recommends a first MMR dose at 12 to 15 months and a second at 4 to 6 years. Babies 6 to 11 months old who will travel internationally should get an early dose, and adults without proof of immunity should get at least one dose, according to the CDC.

Sources indicate that to stop the outbreaks, Moss said the U.S. will need to “increase vaccine coverage, particularly in those communities that have had long-standing low vaccine rates.”.

So far, the response has been “more reactive than proactive,” Moss mentioned. Public health teams scramble once an outbreak starts, he said, and he wants more outreach to at-risk communities before measles arrives.

“I am worried about the ability of the United States to regain measles elimination status in the current climate,” Moss said.

  • Industry observers note that immediately after patch 1.1.3.0 went live, players on PC started reporting massive stutters that would occur every few seconds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There’s been a lot of anticipation for Battlefield 6’s version 1.1.3.0 patch. The patch kicks off the third and final phase of the game’s first season, adding some fresh holiday-themed content. More the new content itself, the enhancement’s biggest additions are almost entirely gameplay-related.

Unfortunately, for as much as the changes in 1.1.3.0 have been well received, the launch has been marred by a series of technical complications, some of which are a little unusual.

Industry observers note that immediately after patch 1.1.3.0 went live, players on PC started reporting massive stutters that would occur every few seconds. The concern is especially pronounced in Redsec Battle Royale, but much deadlier in traditional multiplayer.

Battlefield Studios rapidly acknowledged it, pointing out a workaround that appears to be working for players on Steam. According to those players, going offline on Steam’s friends menu has fixed stuttering for them.

The issue remains for other players on PC, however, and the developer said it’s working on a proper fix.

In a recent development, perhaps the most disrupting problem the patch has caused is one that prevents players from being able to interact with the game’s menu. Tiles become unresponsive, or outright unselectable when you try to hover near them.

Ironically, the top set of tiles designed to make it easy for players to swiftly jump into the new content has been the most affected. Restarting the game sometimes fixes the matter, and some players report that it only happens upon first launch after installing the update.

Recent findings suggest that but Battlefield Studios later clarified that, unsurprisingly, there’s an actual reason behind the bug. Once again, a fix is being investigated, and the developer will offer an revision once some progress has been made.

A little further down the list of importance is an issue that stops players from being able to skip tiers within the newly introduced Winter Offensive bonus path in the game’s battle pass. BF Studios took out the feature entirely while it works on a fix, so while you can continue making progress in the bonus path, you won’t be able to skip tiers.

In a recent development, this is all a shame to see. Outside of all the problems, the meat of the newly introduced update has been almost universally praised. The visibility improvements, and netcode updates have been celebrated. Many players were also happy to see meaningful updates to footstep audio and overall clarity.

Industry observers note that it’s also unusual for a Battlefield 6 patch to run into so many complications at launch. The sentiment around 1.1.3.0 so far is that it’s the game’s best and worst update yet. Hopefully those issues will be fixed before the development team breaks for the holidays.

In a recent development, hyundai’s electric SUVs are getting some love. The IONIQ 5 and three-row IONIQ 9 helped the Korean automaker land its first-ever “Best Electric Vehicle Brand” award from US News & World Report for 2027.

“This win showcases the breadth and strength of Hyundai’s SUV and electric lineups,” Alex Kwanten, managing editor at Autos at US News, said after naming it the Best EV Brand and Best SUV Brand for 2027.

This marks the first time Hyundai has earned the Best EV Brand award and the third consecutive win for Best SUV Brand.

Including hybrid and electric vehicles, Hyundai offers ten unique SUVs, “many of them at or near the top of our rankings in those classes for capability, comfort, performance and value,” Kwanten mentioned.

Hyundai’s fully electric SUVs, the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9, “in particular, stand out for their combination of style and technology,” he explained.

Hyundai currently offers the IONIQ 5, including the sporty IONIQ 5 N and off-road-focused IONIQ 5 XRT, plus the three-row IONIQ 9.

Although Hyundai discontinued its electric sedan, the IONIQ 6, after the 2025 model year, the upcoming high-performance IONIQ 6 N joins the lineup in 2027.

The IONIQ 5 continued to earn praise, taking its third consecutive Best Compact Electric SUV award. Its larger sibling, the IONIQ 9, took the top spot in the midsize electric SUV category.

Hyundai’s IONIQ 5 is the most popular EV in the US this year through September that isn’t a Tesla, ranking third behind the Model Y and Model 3.

Why does it continue winning over buyers? The IONIQ 5 checks all the boxes with long-range capabilities, fast charging, and a surprisingly spacious interior with modern tech.

It’s also among the most affordable EVs in the US. Prices for the 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 start at just $35,250.

However, the base price is for the standard-range IONIQ 5 SE with an EPA-estimated range of up to 245 miles. Upgrading to the extended-range SE RWD model costs an extra $2,500, with prices starting at $37,750, but it offers up to 318 miles of range.

The three-row Hyundai IONIQ 9 electric SUV starts at $58,955 with an EPA-estimated range of up to 335 miles.

Hyundai’s IONIQ 5 is about the size of a Tesla Model Y, with two rows of seating and space for five passengers. Hyundai’s larger IONIQ 9 offers three rows of seating with six- or seven-seat options.

The larger IONIQ 9 offers up to 163.54 cubic feet of interior passenger volume, compared with up to 106.5 cubic feet in the IONIQ 5.

In a recent development, both electric SUVs use an 800-volt electrical architecture for ultra-fast charging. The IONIQ 5 can charge from 10% to 80% in about 20 minutes, while the IONIQ 9 takes around 24 minutes using a 350 kW DC fast charger.

Hyundai assembles the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9 at the Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America outside of Savannah, Georgia.

When we toured the facility earlier this year, Hyundai told Electrek that its electric SUVs are winning over fresh buyers at a higher rate than any of its gas or hybrid vehicles.

Recent findings suggest that the IONIQ 5 had a 69.8% conquest rate last year, while the IONIQ 9 had 64.3%. Hyundai’s Elantra N ranked third (61.9%), followed by the Palisade (61.2%) and Kona Electric (60.9%).

After the death of Shadow’s longtime partner Jackie in August, he had been spotted spending time with the 4-year-old banded female eagle named KD1 (later renamed Kaydee). It seemed like the eagles might head into mating season as a pair, but after the arrival of a new, large female, it’s unclear how the relationships will all shake out.

Sources indicate that since the appearance of the mystery female, nicknamed Big Beautiful Visitor or BBV by some fans, Kaydee has disappeared from view of Friends of Big Bear Valley (FOBBV)’s two cameras. She was last spotted by the cameras on November 14 in the Roost Tree, according to FOBBV. Despite concerns that she may be injured or had left the area, wildlife photographers have continued to document Kaydee’s presence near Big Bear Lake as recently as November 18.

It has been revealed that photographer Alla Shumko shared photos of Kaydee perched near Significant Bear Lake on November 18. Kaydee’s double bands are visible as she observed a scuffle between younger eagles fighting over fish.

In a recent development, mating season is well underway, so viewers of FOBBV’s 24/7 livecams have been watching closely for signs that Shadow has selected a fresh partner. Shadow has worked with both Kaydee and the new eagle on nest maintenance and shared “beaky kisses” with each female, both signs of bonding in bald eagles. Bald eagle mating involves a bit of aerial acrobatics—copulating pairs can be seen in what’s called a “cartwheel display,” in which they lock talons in mid-air while tumbling down to the ground. Male eagles do not have an external phallus, so mating occurs via a touch of cloacas. Vocalizations can typically be heard during the act, which lasts about 7 to 12 seconds, according to Raptor Resource.

In a recent development, as this is nature, we humans can’t predict or influence who Shadow will pick as a new partner. Or if he picks at all. All we can do is watch and wait and let nature take its course.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alpitronic, the company that makes the DC fast chargers used by Ionna, Walmart, Mercedes-Benz, BP Pulse, and others, is building a fresh factory in the United States that will boost output of its 400- and 1,000-kilowatt stalls.

The manufacturer’s fresh 173,315-square-foot facility, located in Fort Mill, South Carolina, will create 70 new jobs and will also act as a testing lab, repair center, logistics hub, and warehouse.

Alpitronic, which has its North American headquarters in Charlotte, North Carolina, and its global headquarters in Bolzano, Italy, said it will invest $33.94 million in the new facility, with $200,000 coming from York County’s Coordinating Council for Economic Development in the form of a Set-Aside grant to assist with the costs of building improvements.

“North America is central to our next phase of growth, and investing in our manufacturing capabilities is key to supporting that expansion,” mentioned Patrik Herrnegger, Alpitronic Americas CEO. “Our Fort Mill facility will put U.S. production under our direct control, bringing us closer to our customers and enabling us to serve them more efficiently. We thank South Carolina and York County for their partnership as we prepare to begin production in early 2027.”.

Recent findings suggest that back in 2024, the tech giant worked with a third-party production partner to open its first local manufacturing facility in Wisconsin. Now, manufacturing has moved in-house, with Alpitronic wholly owning the production operation.

Sources indicate that the upcoming South Carolina plant will assemble HYC400 and HYC1000 stalls, Alpitronic stated. The HYC400 all-in-one dispensers can deliver up to 400 kW of power to a single connected electric vehicle without needing a separate power cabinet, and are the current charger of choice for Ionna and Walmart.

In a recent development, the higher-powered HYC1000 system is composed of a 1,000-kW power cabinet and up to four stalls that can deliver up to 600 kW to a single EV. Each stall can have two ports, and the system can dynamically allocate power to each vehicle to make the best use of the available power.

It has been revealed that what makes the manufacturer's dispensers different from most competitors is the use of silicon carbide components, which lower energy losses and, subsequently, the amount of money EV drivers have to pay for a top-up. According to Alpitronic, SiC modules enable 97.5% efficiency and allow for smaller, quieter, and cooler stalls.

Alpitronic’s new factory in Fort Mill, South Carolina, is scheduled to go online in February 2027.

Tech Report: New Guidelines Recommend Routine Prostate Cancer Screening for Men Over 50

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1000 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As rates of advanced prostate cancer continue to rise, the American Cancer Society (ACS) has issued new guidelines recommending routine prostate cancer screening for many men starting at age 50.
  • The updated recommendations, published November 12 in CA: A Cancer Journal for Clinicians, mark a shift from the organization’s previous emphasis on shared decision making about whether to undergo screening.
  • Under the latest guidelines, the ACS recommends regular prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing beginning at age 50 for men at average risk of prostate cancer and age 45 for those at higher risk.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As rates of advanced prostate cancer continue to rise, the American Cancer Society (ACS) has issued new guidelines recommending routine prostate cancer screening for many men starting at age 50.

The updated recommendations, published November 12 in CA: A Cancer Journal for Clinicians, mark a shift from the organization’s previous emphasis on shared decision making about whether to undergo screening.

Under the latest guidelines, the ACS recommends regular prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing beginning at age 50 for men at average risk of prostate cancer and age 45 for those at higher risk.

Advances in MRI technology and biomarker testing may also help doctors determine which men need further testing, potentially reducing unnecessary biopsies and overtreatment.

The ACS last updated its prostate cancer screening guidelines in 2010, when conflicting research findings raised questions about whether the benefits of PSA screening outweighed the potential harms.

At the time, the organization emphasized informed, shared decision making between patients and healthcare professionals.

However, longer-term follow-up studies have since provided stronger evidence of the benefits of early detection, prompting the ACS to conduct a systematic review and upgrade its recommendations.

The authors of the report noted, “In making these recommendations, we recognize that PSA testing is only the first step in a screening cascade that includes secondary testing of men with an elevated PSA level and treatment decisions for men diagnosed with prostate cancer.”.

The new guidelines recommend a PSA test every 2 years for men ages 50–69 with an average risk of prostate cancer.

The recommendation for those at high risk is a PSA test every year starting at age 45.

Industry observers note that for men ages 70–74, the ACS recommends individualized decision making. If an individual chooses to be screened, the ACS recommends a PSA test every 2 years until the age of 74.

Ramkishen Narayanan, MD, Director of the Center for Urologic Health at The Roy and Patricia Disney Family Cancer Center at Providence Saint Joseph Medical Center in Burbank, CA, who wasn’t involved in the report, told Healthline that screening shouldn’t automatically be ruled out for men over 75.

“[A] point worth noting is that for men over 75, their PSA history as well as their individual clinical scenarios should be evaluated, and that PSA should not be discouraged in this group of men if their life expectancy and clinical history warrant a PSA check.”.

According to the ACS, approximately 1 in 8 men will be diagnosed with prostate cancer during their lifetime.

Individual risk depends on age, race/ethnicity, and other factors:.

Prostate cancer diagnoses in the United States increased by around 3% per year between 2014 and 2022, according to the ACS.

The rise in diagnoses, particularly advanced-stage prostate cancer, has renewed attention on the importance of regular screening.

“[The] current state of prostate cancer screening guidelines is vague and generalized. This has led to ambiguity, disagreement, and variation of opinion among healthcare providers and institutions in their approach to men’s health,” mentioned S. Adam Ramin, MD, board certified urologist, urologic oncologist, and medical director of Urology Cancer Specialists in Los Angeles, CA, who wasn’t involved in the report.

The updated ACS guidelines drew partly on findings from a 2025 follow-up of the European Randomized Study of Screening for Prostate Cancer (ERSPC), which found that regular PSA screening was associated with a 13% reduction in prostate cancer deaths over 23 years.

A 12-year ERSPC follow-up in 2012 also suggested that regular screening was associated with a decrease in metastatic prostate cancer diagnosis, which is another finding that influenced the updated guidance.

“Prostate cancer can take many years, even decades, to become clinically significant, so it takes a long time for us to see the consequences of changes in screening practices,” Taylor Goodstein, MD, assistant professor of urology in the College of Medicine at the University of Cincinnati, who wasn’t involved in the report, told Healthline.

“With longer follow-up from randomized trials, we now have more convincing evidence that PSA screening reduces the risk of dying from prostate cancer,” she noted.

“The ACS guidelines are vital now because they drive home the most important point that prostate cancer screening saves lives,” stated Narayanan.

Healthcare professionals use PSA levels to help determine whether additional testing for prostate cancer may be necessary.

The ACS recommends further testing for men under 70 with PSA levels of 3 ng/mL or higher.

Industry observers note that for those ages 70 and older, the ACS recommends further testing if their PSA is 6.5 ng/mL or higher. This is because PSA levels tend to be naturally higher in older men.

You can speak with your healthcare professional to find out more about PSA cutoff levels.

Goodstein told Healthline that the ways this newly introduced guidance can change the outlook for prostate cancer are simple.

“If we screen men, we can catch troublesome cancers early, before they have a chance to spread,” she said.

Goodstein also emphasized how much the evaluation process has changed. In the past, an elevated PSA level often led directly to a biopsy.

In a recent development, today, doctors generally repeat the PSA test within two weeks to three months to confirm the result. If PSA levels remain elevated, additional testing, including a prostate MRI or validated biomarker test, can help determine whether a biopsy is necessary.

Narayanan told Healthline, “The new guidelines will hopefully remove any confusion about the value of PSA screening and encourage prostate cancer screening as an integral part of a man’s ‘checkup’.”.

He added that it is worth noting that the DRE (digital rectal exam) adds little value to the initial prostate cancer screening and is no longer something that men should fear.

According to recent reports, “Adoption of this set of specific guidelines standardizes the approach to screening for prostate cancer. It provides a unified effort among all levels of healthcare. It most likely will increase the chances of finding prostate cancer in earlier stages and lead to improved cancer treatment outcomes,” stated Ramin.

And that level of purpose-built engineering is more vital than ever. As vehicles grow heavier and more capable, tires need to do more than simply roll down an interstate. Rooted in American engineering and real-world development, Cooper tires are built to an uncompromising standard that live up to their promises. From the rock-crawling STT Pro to the severe-snow-designated Stronghold AT, the Discoverer® family has earned its reputation through real-world testing from Alaskan ice to jagged mountain trails.

In a recent development, the fresh Cooper Discoverer® HT adapts that rugged all-terrain lineage for long-distance highway cruising, matching heavy-duty capability with quiet, refined composure. While it retains the structural durability to wander down a gravel trail with a trailer in tow, its core mission is maximizing comfort and control across hundreds of miles of open road.

Where many highway tires trade load capability for a soft ride, the Discoverer® HT is engineered to handle both. Straight, reinforced sidewalls provide the structural foundation needed to maintain an optimal contact patch under load. Whether the vehicle is running light or carrying family, gear, and tongue weight, the tire resists deformation, ensuring consistent steering response and predictable roadholding grip in any condition. It’s engineered for drivers whose tires have to hold their own—providing a dependable, hard-working partner that won’t fold when the truck or SUV is pushed to its limit.

Cooper tires also tackle truck and SUV tire performance, with advanced features. Its proprietary 3-D Micro-Gauge Siping incorporates interlocking zig-zag sipes inside the tread blocks. Under heavy braking, sharp turns, or loaded acceleration, these interlocking sipes lock together to stiffen the tread block, to help support responsiveness. Crucially, these sipes run deep into the tread rubber, ensuring that gripping edges are still present to help with traction. That structural integrity backs up an exceptional UTQG treadwear rating of 720 and a 70,000-mile limited treadwear warranty on passenger fitments.

In a recent development, this is the tire for drivers who expect their trucks or suvs to show up for the long haul. Whether that means towing a camper into the backcountry, handling moving-day payloads, or eating up cross-country interstate miles in quiet comfort, the mission remains the same: a single set of tires that balances real-world traction, refined manners, and hard-working capability.

Industry observers note that to fit that wide spectrum of work, Cooper offers the Discoverer® HT across 19 passenger sizes covering 16- to 22-inch wheels (with section widths from 245 to 285 mm), alongside 16 light-truck (LT) options engineered with deeper tread grooves and higher load ratings. Backed by a 45-day satisfaction guarantee and over a century of research and development, the Discoverer® HT delivers what Cooper has always stood for: the quiet confidence that the job was done right.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The time has arrived for another Arc Raiders update, and Embark has certainly delivered. Today’s patch, version 1.6.0, is among the smallest the game has received so far, focusing almost exclusively on disabling map exploits.

Perhaps more important than the patch itself, however, is the announcement the developer made around it.

Recent findings suggest that starting off with patch 1.6.0, it takes out a particular zipline on Stella Montis, the game’s most recent addition ot the map roster. Some players used said zipline to get out of bounds, something the game has been battling on several of its maps.

On Blue Gate, the patch fixes a collision glitch that allowed players to vault through a wall, and fall to their death. The map fixes continue with another on Spaceport Launch Tower, which takes out a gap in collision that players have been able to shoot through.

Recent findings suggest that the last change in this update affects gameplay feel around Arc enemies. Certain materials in the game’s world weren’t blocking their vision - or fire - when they should have, and this has now been fixed.

Recent findings suggest that alongside today’s patch, Embark also unveiled that going forward, we’re going to see fewer patches for Arc Raiders. The game has been getting updates almost every Thursday since it rolled out in late October.

Now that most of the major problems have been fixed, the studio is shifting to a slower patching cadence. Critical fixes will still be issued as soon as they’re developed, but don’t expect a patch each week going forward.

Embark also revealed that patch releases and in-game store rotations will now occur on Tuesdays. You should also expect the next few weeks to be quiet, as members of the team go on holiday breaks.

But, before everyone goes away, the game is going to get one more big revision. The last item on Arc Raiders’ roadmap, revealed in early November, is the Cold Snap event. This is on track for Tuesday, bringing some new content alongside a few other fixes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, less than 400 adult North Atlantic right whales (Eubalaena glacialis) still exist in the wild, making them one of the world’s most critically endangered species. Of those, 20 have officially received spiffy newly introduced names from conservationists at the New England Aquarium’s Anderson Cabot Center for Ocean Life. The researchers curate the annual North Atlantic Right Whale Catalog, and attach personable monikers to a select few baleen cetaceans in order to more easily monitor them. This year, it’s time to wave hello to Dodo, Volcano, and Dolly.

Industry observers note that “Naming right whales is a fun and creative activity for our research community, but it also allows an opportunity to connect with the whales on an individual level,” Amy Warren, an aquarium scientific program officer and name project coordinator, said in Anderson Cabot Center’s announcement. “It can be hard to relate to Catalog #5299, but a whale named Nibbles is bound to be memorable.”.

The 2026 inductees also include Grand Slam (Catalog #3991) and Slide (Catalog #4991). The sister whales have a mother named Fenway (Catalog #2791), who was also named in honor of the Boston Red Sox. Grand Slam earned her fresh name thanks to her three patches of raised tissue known as callosities that resemble the bases on a baseball field. Meanwhile, Slide received their name due to the curved scar on her back that recalls someone sliding through home plate. Other right whale names this year include Goose, Donegal, and even Gonzo for the beloved Muppet.

“Although the names are intended to help researchers at sea, they also give the general public a better understanding of the individual whales,” added Caroline Mowdy, a spokesperson for Whale and Dolphin Conservation (WDC).

According to recent reports, collaborators at the WDC also created some lighthearted, yearbook-esque biographies for each whale. For example, Dolly (Catalog #4191), whose callosity looks strikingly similar to the late, great country singer’s larger-than-life hair, apparently loves the song, “Jolene.” Then again, who doesn’t?

In a recent development, “We see these whales and their families grow each year,” remarked Mowdy. “Knowing them makes the tragedies even more tragic, but it also makes our determination to protect them even stronger.”.

Recent findings suggest that on Monday, the North Atlantic Right Whale Consortium revealed that there are roughly 382 North Atlantic right whales, representing a 1.8 percent drop in population size from the 2024 estimate. Their primary threats remain getting tangled in fishing line and vessel strikes.

However, even amid their struggles, the 2025–2026 right whale calving season saw the most calves born since 2009. A total of 24 calves were born, including a surprising late addition that was spotted in Canada in September.

Industry observers note that also, the electric mobility startup spun off from Rivian, is facing another logistics headache. After delaying deliveries of its futuristic TM-B e-bike, the startup has paused shipments entirely to address some software problems that may lead to problematic charging behavior and phantom battery drain.

According to recent reports, in an email sent to reservation holders, the company apologized for the delay, saying it has identified a few software-based concerns that are impacting some bikes, and that it wants to address the issues before resuming shipments, as first reported by The Verge. A firmware update is in the works, and Also estimates that deliveries will resume in approximately two weeks, with another update scheduled for November 24.

In a recent development, this is the latest setback for the mobility spinoff that made headlines last year with its software-heavy bicycles and four-wheeled quads. The TM-B e-bike was originally scheduled to be shipped in the spring of this year, but customers started receiving their orders months later, leading to a barrage of negative comments on the Also subreddit. This prompted Saul Leiken, the startup’s product manager, to post a 661-word apology letter, in which he attributed the setbacks to strict quality standards and “significant supply chain challenges.”.

In a recent development, an Also e-bike customer who received his e-bike posted a YouTube video showing how the TM-B behaves when the state of charge gets low, and how the battery drains while the bike is not in use. Aaron Draczyski remarked he charged his bike in the garage up to 70%, but the state of charge went down to 30% in 24 hours without any usage. What’s more, when the battery level became critically low, the bike refused to charge, throwing an error message that claimed the battery was not installed, even though it hadn’t been removed.

The Also TM-B is unlike most e-bikes out there. Designed from the ground up as a futuristic mobility vehicle, its pedals are not physically connected to the rear wheels. Instead, the rider spins a generator, which provides power to the battery and the electric motor that turns the rear wheel via a rubber belt.

The battery can be recharged via a USB-C port, there’s a round touchscreen to control all of the bike’s features, and the rider can also use a smartphone app to keep tabs on the bike remotely.

Sources indicate that the base Also TM-B starts at $3,500, but the Launch Edition models, which have yet to be shipped, cost $4,500. Earlier this year, when the startup unveiled the first delays, it threw in one of its Alpha Wave helmets and a $250 credit to spend on accessories.

Kia has come a long way since the Besta EV hit the road, now offering a complete lineup of electric vehicles, from compact SUVs and hatchbacks to vans and three-row SUVs.

In Europe and the UK, Kia’s electric lineup consists of the EV2, EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6, EV9, and PV5 van, but the Korean automaker isn’t done yet.

“With no intention of resting on its laurels,” Kia said, the brand plans to complete development of its first software-defined vehicle (SDV) by the end of 2027, an all-new B-segment EV hatchback.

It didn’t offer any other details on the upcoming EV, but Ted Lee, Kia’s executive vice president and head of global operations, told Auto Express that Kia and Hyundai are co-developing a newly introduced dedicated EV architecture for an upcoming pair of entry-level electric cars.

Expected to arrive as the Hyundai IONIQ 1 and Kia EV1, the new EVs will compete with other entry-level electric cars like the Renault Twingo, which starts at about €20,000.

Lee noted the EV1’s price will be highly competitive not just with other entry-level EVs, but also with small gas-powered cars, with prices expected to start in the €20,000 to €22,000 range, or about $22,000 to $24,000. And that’s without government incentives.

The EV2 starts at just €26,600 ($29,500) in Germany and other European markets as Kia’s current entry-level EV, so the price range would make sense.

While it will be Kia’s cheapest EV, Lee promised it would not cut corners in quality, design, or features.

According to recent reports, as its first SDV, the EV1 will feature Kia and Hyundai Motor’s latest-generation tech and software. Kia said the electric SDV will offer Level 2+ autonomous driving on highways. In 2029, Kia plans to expand to Level 2++, enabling it to operate in cities.

The new EV will also use Hyundai’s SDV architecture (CODA), the Pleos Connect infotainment system, and Gleo AI, an in-vehicle Agenic AI.

What will the EV1 look like? According to Auto Express, the entry-level EV will look a bit sportier and less boxy than the EV2 SUV. It could draw inspiration from the Vision Meta Turismo concept.

It also apparently won’t be based on the Picanto, Kia’s smallest gas-powered car. The Kia EV1 is expected to bring a unique style to the family.

Sources indicate that this is good to see and makes sense, especially in Europe. I don't think Kia can go wrong making vehicles at so many different price points. It allows them to reach different segments and almost literally have something for almost everyone.

While all of Kia’s current EVs feature its ccNC infotainment system with dual 12.3″ instrument display and infotainment screens, plus a 5″ climate control panel, the EV1 could bring a simpler setup.

Sources indicate that like its other electric models, the EV1 is expected to receive the GT treatment. However, as an entry-level model, it may not use a dual-motor all-wheel-drive setup like the others.

It has been revealed that will Kia bring the EV1 to the US? Don’t get your hopes up. Kia has previously mentioned the B-segment hatchback is designed for Europe. It could even be built alongside the EV2 at Kia’s plant in Slovakia.

In a recent development, the good news? The EV3, Kia’s compact electric SUV, is now on sale in the US, starting at just $29,890.

#98140. Newly introduced electric comb from China regrew nearly 100% of hair (in mice)

EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Popsci ↗ Open Full Page

Newly introduced electric comb from China regrew nearly 100% of hair (in mice)

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (796 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A potentially revolutionary electronic comb is generating some pretty hair-raising results.
  • Though the Detangle comb (named after the 2010 Disney film Tangled) hasn’t been tested on humans yet, the Chinese scientist behind its development indicates the eye-grabbing results on our distant genetic cousins suggest it could play a role in the neverending quest to keep those luscious locks just a hair longer.
  • Recent findings suggest that created by a team led by Beihang University in Beijing, the comb initially looks like the chunky plastic kind adorning typical pharmacy aisles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A potentially revolutionary electronic comb is generating some pretty hair-raising results. The experimental comb has been used to successfully restore nearly all the hair in bald test subjects. But don’t chuck out that Rogaine just yet. The comb’s owners were mice with shaved backs.

Though the Detangle comb (named after the 2010 Disney film Tangled) hasn’t been tested on humans yet, the Chinese scientist behind its development indicates the eye-grabbing results on our distant genetic cousins suggest it could play a role in the neverending quest to keep those luscious locks just a hair longer.

Recent findings suggest that created by a team led by Beihang University in Beijing, the comb initially looks like the chunky plastic kind adorning typical pharmacy aisles. However, a closer look at its clear plastic handle reveals a green circuit board. Further down, one can see electrodes embedded in the comb’s teeth, which alternate between long and short. The team says that this height variance makes the comb’s pulsed electric field more than two and a half times stronger than it would be with evenly matched teeth.

Recent findings suggest that the shorter teeth also contain two experimental genetic treatments. One boosts blood vessel growth around the hair follicles. The other treatment  blocks dihydrotestosterone (DHT), a hormone known to shrink follicles. The electric field generated by the comb temporarily opens up skin so the treatments can get inside, reaching up to nine times deeper into the follicle region than a conventional cream.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​.

Researchers performed a variety of tests on mice that had their backs shaved and were given testosterone to mimic pattern baldness. Over 28 days, the balding mice were treated with minoxidil or finasteride (the current standards for medical hair restoration), the comb’s electrical stimulation alone, and the comb combined with an experimental genetic treatment. Mice given finasteride regrew about 50 percent of their hair, while the ones on and minoxidil regrew 70 percent. Those numbers  honestly aren’t  too bad on their own, but the results were even better when Detangle got involved. Mice treated with the comb and both experimental treatments saw a staggering 97.85 percent hair regrowth. And all without having to book a flight to Turkey for a hair transplant.

“[T]hese results demonstrate that electrostimulation via the Detangle system promotes hair growth and follicle regeneration in a safe and effective manner,” the team wrote in their paper published earlier this month in the Nature Communications.

The potential market for a hair regrowing comb is sizable to say the least. Detangle’’s creators say androgenetic alopecia, the scientific term for pattern baldness, affects 1.5 billion people worldwide. Some studies suggest up to 80 percent of men will experience pattern baldness, with  some populations seeing symptoms before the age of 40. Somewhere between one fifth and two fifths of women may also experience pattern hair thinning. And hair isn’t just hair. Social expectations and norms around hair partly explain why hair loss can carry psychological baggage.

Recent findings suggest that scientists and hair care providers know this, of course. Toupees, tonics, and tinctures promising to reverse nature’s balding date back thousands of years. Today, the standard medical treatment usually involves topical minoxidil (the active ingredient in Rogaine) and oral finasteride. Minoxidil generally works, but results vary widely from person to person and it requires constant, ongoing application.

Finasteride is often far more effective, with long-term studies showing it can preserve hair in most men for at least a decade, but it also carries the risk for much more intense side effects. The drug (which saw a surge in popularity thanks to online, telehealth services) has been linked to decreased libido and erectile dysfunction. Some patients have also reported anxiety, depression, and suicidal thoughts. While the side effects are uncommon, the risk presented a potentially steep trade off for a fuller head of hair.

Those intrigued by the comb will unfortunately have to hold out quite a bit longer. The team claims more research is needed before the device is tested on humans and, even then, there’s no guarantee the rodent results will translate. Testosterone-induced hair loss on a shaved mouse back is a far cry from human pattern baldness, which typically creeps in over years.

Recent findings suggest that it’s also worth emphasizing that the electric comb, memorable as it is, wasn’t solely responsible for the best results. The pair of experimental genetic treatments used in the study (called SRD5A2 siRNA and VEGFA plasmids) also need to be tested in humans to ensure they are safe and don’t come with unintended side effects of their own. Wig stores, it seems, will live to see another day.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This article is part of a mental health content series called “Mind Games,” in which Healthline editor Morgan Mandriota draws on personal experience and research to challenge misconceptions, reduce stigma, review trends, and share hot takes and lessons learned about what it means to be mentally well.

Coffee and I don’t exactly have the best relationship.

According to recent reports, my morning cup tends to give me jitters, worsen my anxiety, and keep me up until 2 a.m. if I drink it past noon. As an already anxious human, the last thing I need is to exacerbate my symptoms, even if it’s coming from a delicious source.

Industry observers note that over a year ago, I noticed that my anxiety was higher than usual. I was also tossing and turning and waking up at all hours of the night for weeks on end.

It has been revealed that one night in particular, I woke up every hour for 8 hours. Naturally, I wanted to blame it on the full moon or anything other than my beloved coffee, but alas, I realized that my caffeine consumption was the most likely culprit.

Could I have aimed to set a strict drinking schedule to see if that fixed things? Sure. But instead, I decided to quit cold turkey and undergo an experiment to see how I’d feel going coffee-free for the first time in years.

Recent findings suggest that over the next 8 months, I’d swap my coffee station for a matcha setup, dabble in exotic herbal blends from my local teahouse, and become a self-proclaimed tea connoisseur. Lo and behold, my anxiety eased up, and my sleep quality improved, too.

Industry observers note that fast forward to 4 months ago, when I hopped back on the coffee train. But this time, I’m relying on a handy amino acid to help avoid anxiety and other unwanted side effects: L-theanine.

Health and wellness touch everyone’s life differently. This is one person’s story. The views and opinions expressed are those of the speaker and do not necessarily reflect the views or positions of Healthline Media and should not serve as a substitute for medical advice from a healthcare professional.

Industry observers note that L-theanine is mainly found in green and black tea and one type of wild mushroom. The mental health benefits of L-theanine consumption are an emerging area of research, but one 2024 review found that consuming around 200 to 400 milligrams (mg) may help relieve symptoms in people with anxiety disorders.

Still, anecdotal reports suggest there may be benefits of adding L-theanine to coffee. Over the last 5 years, the combo has been gaining traction on Reddit and TikTok for managing caffeine-related side effects.

Despite an overwhelming amount of rave reviews online, I couldn’t find much research to support these claims, so I spoke with a neurologist to see if they had any thoughts.

“This trend has real science behind it,” noted Fawad Mian, MD, who is board certified in neurology, clinical neurophysiology, and sleep medicine and the founder of Ascend Regenerative.

“Controlled studies show caffeine plus L-theanine improves focus and attention more than caffeine alone, and some suggest it softens caffeine’s side effects, like tiredness, headaches, and blood pressure spikes,” Mian remarked. “It smooths caffeine’s effects but doesn’t erase them, so it’s not a license to drink more coffee,” he added.

With all of this in mind, especially after realizing just how calm I was while drinking black and green teas during my coffee break, I decided to give it a try.

After about 4 months of “testing,” I’ve found that adding L-theanine to my coffee works extremely well for me.

It has been revealed that no more anxiety, scatterbrain, shakiness, or staying up until 3 a.m. And no lifestyle overhaul needed. The supplement, which I prefer in liquid form, has become a seamless addition to my daily routine.

Every morning, I make a fresh batch of French press coffee with (strong) local beans, then I squeeze some L-theanine into my cup.

I’ve noticed that I get the usual coffee benefits like improved focus and concentration, plus a nice, calm, stable energy throughout the day.

Even if I drink it until 2 p.m., I’m fighting to keep my eyes open at night before I finally fall asleep around 10. Perhaps this is because L-theanine may also support quality sleep.

Mindful L-Theanine Drops is the liquid supplement that I use every day.

I add a one-second squeeze (which contains 200 mg of L-theanine) into my morning coffee, then I’m good to go. I even started carrying a bottle in my bag just in case I get a latte from a coffee shop on a whim.

According to recent reports, you can also add it to a glass of water, a cup of tea, or another drink of your choosing. It’s unflavored, so it doesn’t alter the taste of your drinks. Real secret stuff.

Out of curiosity, and because I’m a natural skeptic and overthinker, I asked Mian if my positive experience could be a placebo effect, or if I’m seeing real results.

“Expectation may play a small role, but the effect is biologically plausible,” he noted. “L-theanine boosts calming brain activity that offsets caffeine’s stimulation, and 200 mg matches the doses used in studies.” However, he noted that it doesn’t speed caffeine clearance, so drinking coffee only in the morning still matters for sleep quality.

While L-theanine is generally safe to consume, it’s best to speak with a healthcare professional first, especially if you’re pregnant, nursing, receiving cancer treatment, or taking blood pressure medication or sedatives.

“Choose a third-party tested brand, and if caffeine makes you anxious, cutting back is still the simplest fix,” Mian added.

Recent findings suggest that so, if you’re anything like me and drinking coffee also leads to anxiety and jitters for you, I highly recommend trying this supplement once you get the green light from your doctor. It’s been working for me. It may work well for you, too.

Recent findings suggest that who doesn’t love a good fastback? BYD’s latest Han was spotted completely undisguised, giving us an early look at its sleek design and interior ahead of its expected debut next week.

After launching the flagship Great Han last month, or the “Da Han,” as it’s called in China, BYD is preparing to introduce another new member to the lineup.

BYD already sells the smaller Han, but the electric sedan is due for an overhaul. The new version appeared in a regulatory filing by China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) last month.

According to the filing, the next-generation BYD Han will be available in three battery electric (BEV) and one plug-in hybrid (PHEV) variants.

It has been revealed that the Han EV will offer two single-motor rear-wheel-drive (RWD) options, with an output of 328 hp (245 kW) and 402 hp (300 kW). A dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) version will also be offered, delivering a combined 697 hp (520 kW).

All variants use BYD’s Blade LFP Battery and are expected to be equipped with its five-minute Flash Charging technology.

The PHEV version, on the other hand, uses a 1.5-liter engine and an electric motor with up to 268 hp (200 kW).

Ahead of its expected debut at the Guangzhou Auto Show on November 27, BYD’s newly introduced Han was captured in public without any disguise.

The images sent to Autohome show a design similar to the Great Han and other new Dynasty series vehicles, with its latest “Dragon Face” signature front-end look.

A few things have changed from the current model, including latest headlights and a full-length light bar, while the Chinese symbol moved to the hood.

From the side, the Han features a sleek, fastback silhouette. The vehicle also features a roof-mounted LiDAR to support advanced driver-assistance features. The upcoming Han is expected to feature BYD’s God’s Eye B ADAS system.

Industry observers note that inside, the newly introduced Han adopts BYD’s updated interior design. The new setup includes a floating center infotainment screen and a digital instrument panel behind a three-spoke steering wheel.

The center console is also updated with two wireless phone chargers and cupholders without covers.

Sources indicate that doesn't matter for us here in the USA (for now), but I wish the back was a little more sedan looking with a little more trunk lid. Otherwise, nice car.

BYD’s new Han is 5,156 mm long, 1,969 mm wide, and 1,507 mm tall, with a wheelbase of 3,030 mm, which is 161 mm longer than the current version.

Recent findings suggest that the flagship Great Han is the largest of the series, measuring 5,256 mm long. After launching the Great Han on October 13, BYD sold 4,000 units by November 1.

Since the flagship sedan starts at 235,900 yuan, or about $35,000, the smaller Han will likely be closer to 200,000 yuan ($30,000) or less. The outgoing Han starts at 168,800 yuan ($25,000).

Nearly 1 In 5 Tesla Model Ys Failed Their First German Inspection

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (618 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that ask a used Tesla buyer what they’d like checked first, and I’m pretty sure the battery would come up pretty quickly.
  • Germany’s TÜV analyzed 9.7 million mandatory roadworthiness inspections carried out between July 2025 and June 2026.
  • The Model Y finished last out of 109 models for the second year running.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that ask a used Tesla buyer what they’d like checked first, and I’m pretty sure the battery would come up pretty quickly. After reading what German inspectors found underneath some surprisingly young Model Ys, I’d want to know how the suspension was holding up, too.

Germany’s TÜV analyzed 9.7 million mandatory roadworthiness inspections carried out between July 2025 and June 2026. The most revealing comparison was among cars coming in for their first check, at around three years old. EVs won three of the six vehicle classes, but they also occupied the bottom three spots in the overall ranking.

The Model Y finished last out of 109 models for the second year running. Inspectors found major defects on 18.5% of the Model Ys they checked, up from 17.3% a year earlier and nearly triple the 6.4% average for cars that age. No model in that age group recorded a worse result since the 2015 report. Meanwhile, just 3% of Mazda MX-30 EVs failed, good enough for third overall behind the Mazda CX-60 and Mercedes-Benz GLA.

In a recent development, for the Model Y, inspectors flagged worn suspension joints 24 times as often as they did on comparable cars. They also found defective brake discs on 3.4% of Model Ys, against a 1% average for the age group. Front lighting drew more complaints than usual, too.

Tesla Model Ys covered more miles than average, though. By the time they highlighted up for inspection, the Model Ys had traveled an average of 36,000 miles (58,000 kilometers). The average car in the group had driven 29,200 miles (47,000 km), and the average MX-30 had covered only 16,200 miles (26,000 km). Those Teslas had driven more than twice as far as the Mazdas in roughly the same amount of time.

The MG4 is the first car from a Chinese automaker to appear in the report, and it finished second from the bottom, with a 16% failure rate despite averaging only 23,000 miles (37,000 km). Inspectors flagged brake discs on 10.3% of MG4s, about ten times the average. Suspension defects were also unusually common. Just ahead of the MG was Tesla’s Model 3, with a 12.5% failure rate at an average of 34,200 miles (55,000 km).

In a recent development, the Model Y’s poor performance in Germany runs counter to its reputation for reliability. American buyers may remember that Consumer Reports ranked the Model Y as its most reliable upcoming EV, though that’s based on owners reporting the problems they’d encountered.

Technical inspections, on the other hand, may find play in a suspension joint that the driver hasn’t noticed. There’s also a difference between buying new and buying used, even in Consumer Reports’ own data. Tesla finished last as a brand in its separate survey of five- to ten-year-old cars, which is perhaps more telling.

The German results apply to the Model Y that preceded the Juniper refresh. When I drove the updated Model Y, the softer suspension and upcoming frequency-selective dampers made it noticeably more comfortable. Whether this softer suspension setup holds up better is something we’ll learn as those cars cover more miles.

Sources indicate that if you’ve been following the game’s development, you’ll know that it was pretty clear we’re closer than ever to the official launch. The most recent beta build highlighted off polished content, with new animations and cutscenes.

It has been revealed that we’ve been playing it ourselves, and we think you’re going to agree with our Arknights: Endfield character tier list. You can expect more coverage from us as we get closer to launch, and when the game actually arrives.

Though it might seem like it came out of nowhere, the game is based on the Arknights universe, itself a massive mobile game with over 100 million downloads. Endfield brings a different flavour to that world, with a mix of strategy, exploration and real-time combat, not unlike the many games created by HoYoverse.

You can pre-register yourself on the official website.

How to Plan Your Holiday Meals in a Year of Unprecedented Recalls
